action_summary: Rounds 9-12 built produce-a-kind and judge-a-kind, and by round 12 the machine read 98.2% of a real system. Before building round 13 on the same pattern, I tested the STRATEGY those rounds assume: that one demonstration per environment plus a published guide totals computer use. The tree already held the numbers, so no new episode was run. Three new measurements over the recorded 78-task run: (1) the cost of an UNSEEN step moves 5.49 -> 5.39 bits, a change of -0.10 across the whole run, which is FLAT at a stated 0.25-bit threshold; (2) 90.3% of the bill sits in three attributes (tag, classes, id) that each name an element, with zero conjunctions, so the smaller-language lever the tree named is already spent; (3) 63% of real steps face more than 30 candidate descriptions, so the price is set by page density and no learner can lower it by seeing more pages. Verdict: the strategy is RETRACTED as a total answer. What survives is narrower and real: each experience permanently removes about one bit.

agent_orientation.earlier_routes_exhausted_reason: Three routes rejected. (1) Build round 13 as another judge: rounds 11-12 already read 98.2% of a real system, so the judge layer is not what limits capability, and building more would optimise a claim just measured false. (2) Shrink the description language: tested, 90.3% of the bill is in three attributes that each name an element, so removing one removes the ability to say what a step targets. (3) Lower the bits with a better learner: the cost is log2 of what the page does not distinguish, which no learner lowers by seeing more pages.
agent_orientation.independent_verification_note: Producer-run sandbox only: 9 new tests including two synthetic receipts that must flip the verdict. One receipt: 5.49 -> 5.39 bits per step (FLAT at a 0.25-bit threshold), 90.3% of the bill in three necessary attributes, 63% of steps above 30 candidates, and the strategy retracted as a total answer. No independent identity has re-run any of it.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: OSWorld 2.0's authors diagnose frontier failure as weak recovery and maintenance of hidden state. A computer-use agent's action is only as good as the invocation it can compose from what the environment declares. Round 7 measured that the composition was wrong for reasons the environment had already published: the same 20 programs yield 33 doors when their declarations are misread and 57 when they are read, with no new knowledge acquired. No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
